display.purpose: Page and section headlines, product names. Mixed case, italic-in-brand-color for emphasis.

label.purpose: Category tags, form labels, small metadata. Used sparingly, never as a persistent chrome strip.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid burgundy CTA (add to cart, view details, quote).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.8rem 1.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; background: #7c0000; color: #ffffff; border: none; box-shadow: 0 8px 20px -10px hsl(43 25% 20% / 0.55); transition: transform 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease, background-color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #560000; box-shadow: 0 10px 24px -8px hsl(43 25% 20% / 0.6); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7c0000; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0.8rem 1.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; background: #fffdf8; color: #2b211d; border: 1.5px solid #d8c3ae; transition: border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: #7c0000; color: #7c0000; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7c0000; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Yume's visual system reads like a real desk drawer of a small stationery studio: pieces of paper, stickers, and printed samples set down slightly askew, not squared to a grid. Warmth comes first, precision second, order a distant third. The palette stays close to the material it sells (paper, warm cream, a single deep burgundy ink), typography leans on a real serif rather than a system sans, and the layout tolerates gentle imperfection (a card tilted a degree or two) rather than enforcing machined alignment. This is a deliberate reversal of an earlier Swiss-editorial pass on this same project (bold grotesk display type, mono-caps chrome, sharp 0-radius corners, numbered index cards, a black inversion block) — that direction is a confirmed anti-reference: nothing in this system should drift back toward it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper background, never stark white or pure black
One accent color only (burgundy), used deliberately and sparingly
Soft, generous corner radius everywhere; no sharp rectangles
Warm-tinted low-alpha shadows instead of hard borders on content surfaces
A subtle, consistent tilt on card grids for a handmade, non-machined feel
Serif display type (Playfair Display) paired with a plain sans body (Inter)

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Burgundy is the only saturated color on the page. Every other surface is warm neutral (paper, ink, blush tint). A second accent hue is never introduced.

rules.name: The One Emphasis Rule
rules.body: To emphasize a word inside a serif headline, use italic of the same family in the brand color. Never mix in a second typeface for emphasis.

rules.name: The No-Stack Rule
rules.body: A surface is either shadow-elevated (content: cards, photos, buttons) or hairline-structural (chrome: header, footer, dividers). Never both on the same element.

dos: Do use warm-tinted shadows (hsl(43 25% 20% / …)) for every card/button shadow — never a neutral or pure-black shadow.
Do keep burgundy as the only saturated accent color on any page.
Do use full-pill radius for every button and small tag, 1.25rem for cards/frames.
Do apply the tilt-a/tilt-b alternation to any new card grid with 2+ items.
Do keep body copy in Inter and any headline/product-name in Playfair Display.
donts: Don't reintroduce sharp (0-radius) corners, mono-caps uppercase chrome strips, numbered index cards, or a black/inverted section — all confirmed anti-references from the Swiss-editorial pass this system replaced.
Don't stack a border and a shadow on the same card or frame.
Don't introduce a second accent hue (no blue, no green, no purple) even for a single small element.
Don't use pure #000000 or pure #ffffff anywhere.
Don't make the tilt effect stronger than about a degree, or apply it to a single isolated card outside a grid.
